project: PRD-266 W3 Store duties — Automatos Go backend: content reports, AI providers for the consent sheet, paused tasks in the calendar, universal-link files and /go/pair (one branch, one PR, one CI run)
description: PRD-266 (docs/PRDS/PRD-266-AUTOMATOS-GO-BACKEND.md, on main since #1257) wave W3 (Store duties): US-016, US-017 and US-018 re-cut into 10 stories that each fit one session, in dependency order (K2). US-019 is not in this kit (it needs W1's mobile_devices table and pairing routes; it moves to the W2 kit). US-018's chat-history paging is W1's US-007b (K3). Backend + web; NO Alembic revision (K4); no new dependency; no third-party client. Built in parallel with W1 (K5). Diff base for every check: `bash scripts/ralph/acceptance-prd266w3.sh --print-base`.
decisions: D10–D11 (PRD-266 decisions.md): iOS first; Android testers install EAS internal builds from a link (no Play Console yet). App name Automatos Go; bundle id com.automatos.app.
D15 (§3): 'Report this' goes to the workspace owner (in-app notification) and an Automatos moderation inbox; on a self-hosted install to its operator only.

D23 (§3): a one-time AI consent sheet before the first message names the providers; the server tells the app which providers it uses (the PRD chose GET /api/workspaces/current); shown again when the list changes.
D27 (decisions.md): calendar pause is for routines and agent-scheduled tasks; paused scheduled tasks stay in the feed, greyed, instead of vanishing.
D51 (decisions.md): WebSummit testers are the team's phones only, on internal TestFlight; no store listing exists yet.
D63 (§3, revises D7): the app deletes nothing; US-015 is withdrawn. Deleting a workspace stays in Studio, unchanged.

§4.8: content reports are POST /api/v1/reports {target_type: message | deliverable, target_id, reason, note?}: an audit row (core/workspaces/audit.py, event content_reported, NO new table), a new in-app event content_reported to the workspace owner, and on SaaS a summary to MODERATION_WEBHOOK_URL (unset on self-hosted installs, so only the operator sees it). Owners list reports from the existing audit view.

§4.8: GET /api/workspaces/current adds ai_providers: [{id, name}]: the providers whose models this workspace's Auto and agents can call (platform routes plus the workspace's own keys) and the embeddings provider.

§4.9: paused scheduled tasks stay in GET /api/activity/schedule with paused: true; GET /api/chat/history honours starting_after; apple-app-site-association and assetlinks.json are served by the frontend on ui.automatos.app for /go/*, /command-center and /chat, app id KGVA9933BG.com.automatos.app.

§4.10 files already over AGENTS.md's 800-line limit may NOT grow. This wave touches api/workspaces.py (985) and services/activity_service.py (1,309); it never touches main.py (1,684), core/auth/hybrid.py (954), api/chat.py (908), consumers/chatbot/service.py (3,074) or frontend/lib/api-client.ts (3,921). The one named exception: orchestrator/config.py gains its settings line, and the generated reports route-manifest.json and config-surface.json gain their entries.

§4.10 code shape on every changed line: functions under 50 code lines, nesting under 4, cyclomatic complexity under 10, new files 200–400 lines (never over 800), type hints and docstrings on public functions, no mutation of arguments, no swallowed errors; settings only through config.py with each name in reports/config-surface.json (no os.getenv/os.environ elsewhere, ruff TID251); no hardcoded values (named constants or config).

§4.10 'stop and ask first' (#1255, approved by Gerard 20 Oct): this wave changes no authentication, permission or tenancy rule. POST /api/v1/reports is gated by the existing require_workspace_permission; the only new unauthenticated surfaces are three frontend paths (the two app-association files and the static /go/pair page), listed in the saas middleware as PRD-264 did for /verify. No new public backend route, no new third-party client, no new dependency.

K1 (kit): branch feat/prd-266-w3-store-duties, cut from origin/main (7ae677b52 on 20 Oct, which carries the PRD: #1257 merged), worktree <workspace>/.worktrees/automatos-ai/feat+prd-266-w3-store-duties. The wave's PR targets main and is 'Part of #1255' (not Closes: US-019 is still to come). The diff base for every check is what `bash scripts/ralph/acceptance-prd266w3.sh --print-base` prints (the merge-base with origin/main).

K2 (kit): this kit is US-016, US-017 and US-018 only, re-cut into ten one-session stories in dependency order (US-016a → US-016b → US-016c → US-017a → US-017b → US-017c → US-018a → US-018b → US-018c → US-018d). US-019 (Phones & devices in Studio) is NOT here: it needs W1's mobile_devices table and pairing routes (feat/prd-266-w1-connect, unmerged) and moves to the W2 kit, stacked on W1. US-015 is withdrawn (D63).

K3 (kit): US-018's chat-history AC ('starting_after pages chat history, if not done in US-007') is W1's US-007b, which W1's kit builds on feat/prd-266-w1-connect tonight. This wave never touches api/chat.py or consumers/chatbot/service.py (both W1's and both over 800 lines). If W1 lands without it, where it goes is the lead's call.

K4 (kit): NO MIGRATION. Reports are audit_logs rows (the PRD's 'no new table'; #1255 rejected a reports table), the owner's notice a notifications row, paused tasks already have agent_scheduled_tasks.status = 'paused', workspace keys are user_api_keys rows. The gate refuses any new revision and any change to the two head pins, so W1's new head prd266_mobile_devices never meets a second head at merge.

K5 (kit): W1 builds in parallel on feat/prd-266-w1-connect. Expected merge seams, resolved by whichever PR merges second: orchestrator/reports/route-manifest.json (both add routes and bump route_count; 945 on this base), orchestrator/reports/config-surface.json (W1's MOBILE_* names and MODERATION_WEBHOOK_URL are neighbours in sorted order), orchestrator/router_manifest.py (both append a RouterSpec at the end of MANIFEST_ROUTERS), orchestrator/config.py (different sections). Two cross-wave pieces cannot be built on this base and are merge items: discovery's report_content capability (W1 owns services/mobile/discovery.py, whose test maps every capability to a live route) and an exemption for /go/pair in W1's 'Pair this browser' gate (US-005b replaces the whole app in local paired mode when no token is stored). This wave never creates or edits a W1 file: services/mobile/, api/mobile_devices.py, api/well_known.py, core/auth/pairing.py, core/auth/bearer_registry.py, core/auth/device.py, core/models/mobile_devices.py, components/settings/phones-devices/, core/security/rate_limiter.py, core/security/ip_bucket.py, api/voice_retell.py and modules/voice/ (W1's US-008a/b; US-017b only reads modules/voice/live_settings.py).

K6 (kit): the new router registers through RouterSpec('api.content_reports') in orchestrator/router_manifest.py (as api.cli_hosts and api.provenance do; W1's K3), so main.py never changes. This supersedes §4.10's 'registered in main.py', for the same reason as in W1: main.py is 1,684 lines.

K7 (kit): module names. Content reports live in the package services/content_reports/ (targets.py, service.py, moderation.py), NOT services/reports/ as §4.10 says: 'reports' in this codebase is PRD-76's agent reports (api/reports.py at /api/reports, services/report_service.py, api.add_report_to_knowledge). The router is api/content_reports.py at /api/v1/reports, as the PRD names it. The provider list is one module, services/ai_providers.py. The schedule source moves to services/activity_scheduled_task_items.py (the services/activity_social_items.py precedent).

K8 (kit): the report contract. Body {target_type: 'message' | 'deliverable', target_id (1–64 characters), reason: one of REPORT_REASONS = harmful, offensive, inaccurate, privacy, other, note?: ≤ 500 characters}; extra fields refused. The reason list is a kit choice (the PRD and the app's PRD-001 say only 'reason and an optional note'); the app's picker follows it. Any member may report, a viewer included (FR-15), through require_workspace_permission('members:read'), which every role holds; a caller with no resolvable person (an API key, an SDK key) is 403. A message target is an assistant message in the caller's workspace, in a chat the reporter owns or a public chat; a deliverable target is one DeliverableService.get_deliverable finds in the caller's workspace; anything else is 404, never 403. The audit row: action content_reported, resource_type = target_type, resource_id = target_id, user_id = the reporter, details {reason, note, excerpt (≤ 200 characters)}. A second report of the same target by the same reporter answers 200 with the first report's id and sends nothing. Each reporter is rate-limited (check_rate_limit, subject = the reporter, limits from config.rate_limit_for('content_report', 20, 3600)); DEFAULT_LIMITS is untouched (W1 edits that dict). A new report answers 201 {report_id, status: 'received'}.

K9 (kit): the owner's notice. Event content_reported (added to VALID_EVENT_TYPES), user_id = the owner's users.id (core/workspaces/owner.workspace_owner; the operator on a local install), link_type 'content_report' (the bell opens Command Center → Governance, which holds the Audit pane), title 'Content reported', a message naming the target kind and the reason only, never the excerpt or the note. No owner found → no notice at all (a user_id NULL row would reach every member), logged at WARNING; the report still stands.

K10 (kit): the moderation post and PRD open question 2. The setting MODERATION_WEBHOOK_URL is config, so OQ2 (which inbox, who answers) does not block the build: nothing posts until Gerard sets it on Railway. It posts only when AUTH_EDITION=saas AND the setting is an https URL; a local install posts nothing even when it is set (D15). It is sent through the existing generic webhook driver (channels/drivers/webhook.py: httpx, 15 s timeout, body {text, message, ai_generated: true}; the excerpt is AI output), after the response (FastAPI BackgroundTasks), for a new report only. The text carries the report id, the workspace id, the target type and id, the reason, the excerpt (≤ 200 characters) and the note (≤ 200 characters); never the reporter's name, email or id, never the workspace's name. The URL is a credential: never logged, and the driver's error text (an httpx exception can quote the URL) is never logged verbatim.

K11 (kit): ai_providers = [{id, name}], sorted by id and unique; ids are provider-registry slugs (core/llm/providers.py, stable), names the registry labels. Sources: (a) the workspace's own keys: active user_api_keys rows of this workspace whose byok_overrides switch is on (key_resolver._byok_key's lane), chat providers only; (b) platform routes: every chat provider that platform_key_allowed for this edition and has a platform key present (an active row in PLATFORM_KEY_WORKSPACE_ID's user_api_keys when set, the credential store under the four names api/user_api_keys.get_platform_key_status reads, or the config env key); (c) the embeddings provider (the system setting embeddings.provider, else config.EMBEDDING_PROVIDER; unset, 'disabled' and 'huggingface_local' add none); (d) the RAG reranker, Cohere, when config.RAG_RERANK_ENABLED and core/llm/rerank_manager says a key is configured (the reranker receives the user's query: D23's 'your messages are sent to them'; a kit addition for the lead to confirm); (e) local edition with CLI_RUNTIME_ENABLED: the CLI runtime of every agent of this workspace that runs as a session, named by its core/cli_presets label (Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot) with the preset's usage slug as id; (f) Retell (id 'retell', name 'Retell AI', named constants) when the workspace can use Auto Live voice, because Auto Live sends the user's audio to Retell, a third-party AI (Apple 5.1.2(i); coordinator, 20 Oct). 'Can use' is the mint route's own gates minus the monthly cap (a capped workspace is still a Retell user this month): the platform switch modules/voice/live_settings.voice_live_enabled() (system setting voice.live_enabled), Retell armed (retell_credentials().armed: key, webhook secret and agent id present), the workspace's own switch (parse_workspace_voice_live(workspace.settings).enabled), and on SaaS the plan (D34: services/plan_tiers.exposure_for_plan(plan).families.voice true, or a known tier that declares no families policy, enterprise today: the rule W1's US-008a enforces at the mint on its branch); local is never plan-gated. It reads key PRESENCE only: no user_api_keys key is decrypted and no key value (the Retell key included) is returned, logged or cached. A read failure answers ai_providers: null, logged with logger.exception; GET /api/workspaces/current still answers.
K12 (kit): ai_providers is NOT added to discovery (decisions.md D23 allowed either; the PRD chose /api/workspaces/current; discovery is public and W1's, and one workspace's providers are not public).

K13 (kit): paused tasks. Agent-scheduled task items with status active or paused carry paused (bool); cancelled never appear; other sources are unchanged; one execute() per call as today. A paused recurring task shows at its next cron slot (where it would run), a paused one-off at its next_run_at. The web calendar reads the same feed, so it changes in the same wave: a paused item is greyed with the word 'Paused', offers Resume and Cancel instead of Pause, and Next up skips it. Auto's platform_get_schedule tool reads the same feed and sees paused: true (no change there).

K14 (kit): universal-link files are Next.js route handlers, frontend/app/.well-known/apple-app-site-association/route.ts and frontend/app/.well-known/assetlinks.json/route.ts (application/json, 200, no redirect), listed as exact paths in the saas middleware's public routes, served in both editions (a self-hosted web address is not one of the app's associated domains, so the files are inert there). AASA: appIDs [KGVA9933BG.com.automatos.app], components /go/*, /command-center, /command-center/*, /chat, /chat/*. assetlinks: package com.automatos.app; sha256_cert_fingerprints from the frontend server env ANDROID_APP_SHA256_CERT_FINGERPRINTS (comma-separated, each AA:BB:… validated); none set → [] (open question: the EAS Android signing certificate's SHA-256). No next.config.js change.

K15 (kit): /go/pair is a public page (saas middleware, exact path like /verify), no app shell, no sign-in, and NO API call of any kind: it never pairs. It repeats the code and the server it pairs with (each validated before it is shown), says how to get Automatos Go (in testing for invited testers: TestFlight on iPhone, an install link on Android; one constant holds the copy for when a store listing exists), and tells the reader to open Automatos Go and scan from inside the app, or type the address and the code. PRD finding: a self-hosted web address is never one of the app's associated domains and pairing exists only on local installs, so a QR scanned with the phone's camera ALWAYS lands on this page; the in-app scanner is what pairs. HOST_OWNED_ROUTES (PRD-261's theme contract, TS and Python with a parity test) is unchanged: /go is outside PAGE_SCOPE and /x, so no theme can serve it.

K16 (kit): the gate compares three long functions with the base, byte for byte: NotificationDispatcher.dispatch (129 code lines; VALID_EVENT_TYPES is a module constant beside it), EmbeddingManager._load_provider (59) and get_request_context_hybrid (136, never touched by this wave). get_current_workspace (45 code lines) stays ≤ 50; ActivityService._scheduled_task_items (44) moves out and becomes a delegate.

K18 (kit): ONE push, ONE PR, ONE CI run. Story commits end ' [skip ci]'; the runner pushes the branch as a backup after each session (no PR exists, so nothing runs) and opens the wave's draft PR once the build is COMPLETE. No story waits on CI; nothing runs on the owner's machine.

K19 (kit): gitleaks scans every push: no test or doc holds a Slack-webhook-shaped URL (hooks.slack.com/services/…) or any real-looking credential; fixtures use https://moderation.example.test/… (the gitleaks fixture trap).

K20 (kit): the global secrets hook refuses Write/Edit on any path matching *.env, *.env.*, */.env, */.env.*, */credentials*, */secrets/*, */secret/*, *.pem, *.key, *_rsa, *_rsa.pub, */service-account*.json, */sa-key*.json. Every path this kit names was scanned against those on 20 Oct: none matches. Never write an .env or .env.example file (document a variable in docs/deployment-infrastructure/environment-variables.md instead). The PRD on this base still names core/auth/credentials.py (W1 renamed it core/auth/bearer_registry.py on its branch): this wave writes neither. Never work around the hook; a story that seems to need such a path stops RALPH_BLOCKED.

service.py file_report(db, ctx, *, target_type, target_id, reason, note) returns a frozen result (report_id, duplicate, and the fields the moderation post needs) and raises ReportNeedsAPerson (no person: core.auth.principal.resolve_user_pk is None), ReportTargetNotFound or ReportNotRecorded. (f) Retell: {id: RETELL_PROVIDER_ID = 'retell', name: RETELL_PROVIDER_NAME = 'Retell AI'} (named constants) is listed exactly when the workspace can use Auto Live voice: modules.voice.live_settings.voice_live_enabled() (the platform switch, system setting voice.live_enabled) AND retell_credentials().armed (key, webhook secret and agent id present: only .armed is read, the key is never kept, logged or returned) AND parse_workspace_voice_live(workspace.settings).enabled (the workspace's own switch) AND, on AUTH_EDITION=saas only, the plan allows voice (D34): services.plan_tiers.exposure_for_plan(workspace.plan or 'basic') has families.voice true, or the workspace's plan is a known tier that declares no families policy (enterprise today), the rule W1's US-008a enforces at the mint on its branch; local is never plan-gated.
